Survival dropout implementation contract (step 2)

\subsection{Observed dropout proportions for survival trials}
\label{fs:survival:dropoutProportions}
Enrollment, event time, and exponential dropout time are independent within each
arm. The input dropout probability $d_g$ at time $t_D$ specifies the hazard
$\phi_g=-\log(1-d_g)/t_D$; it is not an observed dropout proportion.
For follow-up $u\geq0$, the observed dropout incidence is
\[
 F_{D,g}(u)=\int_0^u\phi_g\exp(-\phi_g x)S_g(x)\,dx.
\]
Events compete with dropout. Exponential and piecewise exponential event hazards
are supported; the Weibull/nonzero-dropout extension is deferred.

Analytic planning conditions on deterministic piecewise constant accrual and
planned allocation. Fractional planned counts are retained without rounding.
For interval $[a_j,a_{j+1}]$ and arm-specific intensity $r_{g,j}$, let
$c_j(t)=\min(t,a_{j+1})$ and
$n_{g,j}(t)=r_{g,j}\max(0,c_j(t)-a_j)$. For $n_g(t)=\sum_j n_{g,j}(t)>0$,
\[
 q_g(t)=\sum_{j:n_{g,j}(t)>0}\frac{n_{g,j}(t)}{n_g(t)}
 \frac{\int_{a_j}^{c_j(t)}F_{D,g}(t-a)\,da}{c_j(t)-a_j}.
\]
The denominator includes only subjects accrued by the horizon. Constant planned
allocation scales numerator and denominator equally within an arm.
\texttt{getSampleSizeSurvival()} and \texttt{getPowerSurvival()} report
\texttt{expectedDropoutProportion1} and \texttt{expectedDropoutProportion2}
as derived probabilities, one per alternative scenario without a stage dimension,
at that scenario's final planned analysis time. No early-stopping weighting is
used. An unavailable final horizon or zero accrued arm count gives NA; otherwise
zero dropout gives zero.

Patient-wise two-arm, multi-arm, and enrichment survival simulation retains the
existing recruitment and allocation mechanisms. In replication $r$, each arm or
population finishes at its last contributing analysis $T_{r,g}$, including the
analysis of discontinuation. Shared control uses its last applicable analysis;
overlapping enrichment populations retain their membership. Count dropout only
before the event and by $T_{r,g}$, with denominator $N_{r,g}(T_{r,g})$ enrolled
subjects. Average $D_{r,g}/N_{r,g}$ over replications with a usable horizon and
positive denominator, rather than pooling counts. Report the corresponding mean
horizon over exactly these replications. The field stems are
\texttt{observedDropoutProportion} and \texttt{dropoutObservationTime}; labels are
``Observed dropout proportion'' and ``Dropout observation time''. Retain contributor
counts internally. Both summaries are NA if no replication contributes.
These outputs are unavailable for test-statistic-based simulation. Comparisons
with analytic results require matching horizon, enrollment and allocation assumptions.

Verification acceptance criteria

\subsubsection{Survival dropout proportion verification}
\label{tp:survival:dropoutProportions}
Requirements: FS Sec.~\ref{fs:survival:dropoutProportions}.
Analytic checks cover zero dropout, exponential closed forms, unequal allocation
and arm-specific dropout, fractional counts during accrual, zero enrollment,
piecewise accrual and event hazards at and around boundaries. Compare with
independent quadrature (absolute error below $10^{-8}$) and a competing-risk
simulation on a fixed discrete enrollment schedule (within five Monte Carlo
standard errors); assess continuous/discrete enrollment approximation separately.
For both APIs verify final-stage horizon selection, fixed and sequential designs,
multiple scenarios, missing final horizons, derived classification and labels
without stage indices. Existing event counts, sample sizes, power and times must
remain unchanged.

Simulation checks cover all three patient-wise APIs, unequal and zero dropout,
empty denominators and no eligible replications, multiple arms/scenarios,
overlapping enrichment populations, early stopping and selection. Reconstruct
counts at each arm/population's finishing horizon, including discontinued groups
and shared control. Check contributor counts, averaging replication-specific
proportions rather than pooled counts, and mean horizons over identical eligible
replications. Test-statistic simulation must not report these summaries.
Analytic comparisons require matching fixed horizons, enrollment and allocation,
with Monte Carlo uncertainty separated from accrual approximation.
